name: VexelRay
description: Desktop applications built on the VexelRay stack: a file explorer, a text editor, an image viewer, a terminal, a calculator, and fluid and rigid-body simulations. They are separate programs that know about each other, so a file in the explorer opens in the editor or the viewer, and the editor can show a file in the explorer.

site.tagline: Seven desktop applications drawn live on the GPU, which know about each other. One line installs them all.
site.requirements: Needs Windows 10 or 11 (64-bit) and a graphics card with an up-to-date driver: everything here draws with Vulkan.

sections.title: Built different, underneath
sections.lede: Every application above runs on the same framework, and it does things you would not expect from a desktop toolkit.

cards.title: Frames only on demand
cards.text: A window draws when something changes and sleeps when nothing does, waking to its first frame in about a millisecond. The whole window is one draw call.

cards.title: Multithreaded by default
cards.text: The main thread only draws. App logic, disk work and time run on their own lanes, placed at compile time, so a part that hangs never freezes the window.

cards.title: A clock you can test
cards.text: Kronometer drives every animation from one logical clock. On its virtual clock, a ten-minute scenario runs in microseconds, identically every time.

sections.title: Build your own
sections.lede: VexelRay is also a framework: Java 25, compiled to a native Windows executable and drawn with Vulkan. Every application above is built on it. Yours can be too, whether a coding agent writes most of it or you write all of it.

cards.title: Start from the template
cards.text: One command generates a working application with tabs, a file navigator, settings that persist, and tests that build the window without a GPU. Vex, Calculator and MainFrame all started this way.

cards.title: Build it with an LLM
cards.text: The stack was written with Claude Code. The framework and the GUI carry a `CLAUDE.md` with the rules the code does not show, and every generated project starts with one. `ottermate` lets a coding agent drive and screenshot the window it built, so it checks its own work by looking at it.

cards.title: Or write it yourself in Vex
cards.text: Vex highlights Java, jumps to any declaration in your project or in the framework, and shows a folder's Maven modules before you open it. MainFrame and Vexplore work alongside it.

sections.title: Built with
sections.lede: VexelRay would not exist without three pieces of other people's work, and we're grateful for each of them.

cards.title: Claude Code, by Anthropic
cards.text: Most of VexelRay was written with Claude Code, Anthropic's coding agent, working alongside its author. Ottermate exists so Claude can see the windows it builds.

cards.title: Oracle GraalVM
cards.text: Oracle GraalVM's Native Image compiles every application ahead of time into a single Windows executable that runs without a JVM.

cards.title: Vulkan, by the Khronos Group
cards.text: Everything here is drawn with Vulkan, the open, cross-platform graphics and compute API from the Khronos Group, with every shader compiled to SPIR-V.
